planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part shade; Sea Bilberry fruits best with some sun but tolerates considerable shade as an evergreen understory shrub.

directions: Plant in part shade on acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; Sea Bilberry is an East Asian evergreen huckleberry relative bearing white racemes of small bell-shaped flowers followed by edible black berries. It tolerates light shade well, though fruiting is heaviest with at least some direct sun through the day. Its evergreen foliage and tidy habit also make it a worthwhile landscape shrub beyond its fruiting value, suited to a woodland-edge planting in zones 7-9.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade; Himalayan Huckleberry is one of the more shade-tolerant Vaccinium species, per the Royal Horticultural Society.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade on acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; Himalayan Huckleberry is an evergreen shrub with distinctive glaucous, grey-white leaf undersides, bearing white, bloomed black berries following small white flowers. The Royal Horticultural Society notes it tolerates full shade, partial shade, or sun equally well, making it one of the more flexible Vaccinium species for a shaded woodland garden. Its ornamental foliage color contrast adds year-round interest beyond the fruiting display.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Azores Blueberry is semi-evergreen and holds foliage longer than many deciduous Vaccinium species.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade on acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; Azores Blueberry is a semi-evergreen woodland-garden shrub native to the Azores, bearing pink-white bell flowers followed by edible black berries. It is hardy to roughly -10 to -5°C (RHS H4), and the Royal Horticultural Society explicitly recommends growing it in sun or partial shade. Reaching 3 to 13 feet depending on age and site, it makes a substantial woodland-edge specimen with both ornamental flowers and a genuine fruit crop.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, peaty, lime-free soil in partial to light shade; Caucasian Whortleberry is documented fruiting heavily even in fairly heavy shade at UK arboreta.

directions: Plant in partial to light shade on acidic, peaty, lime-free soil; Caucasian Whortleberry is a deciduous woodland shrub native to the Caucasus region, growing considerably larger than common garden blueberries at up to 15 feet. It has been documented fruiting heavily even in fairly heavy shade at established UK arboreta such as Westonbirt, making it a good choice for a shaded woodland garden wanting genuine fruit production rather than just ornamental foliage. Keep soil consistently moist and acidic, as with other Vaccinium species, and avoid any lime amendment.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Madeiran Blueberry is a niche specialty-nursery item, source from a vendor carrying Macaronesian endemics.

directions: Plant in partial shade on acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; Madeiran Blueberry is a Macaronesian endemic from the laurel forests of Madeira, a woodland-understory shrub that fruits heavily at a relatively small size with tangy medium-sized berries. It has thinner nursery availability than mainland Vaccinium species, typically found only through specialty collector nurseries, but is a genuine and distinctive shade-tolerant fruiting shrub for a protected zone 8-10 garden. Give it the same acidic, moisture-retentive soil as other blueberry relatives and protect from hard freezes.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; this small evergreen alpine-woodland shrub is often used as a groundcover-scale planting.

directions: Plant in partial shade on acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil; Himalayan Dwarf Blueberry is a small evergreen shrub from Himalayan and Chinese alpine-woodland habitats, grown both as an ornamental groundcover-scale shrub and for its edible fruit. Its low, spreading habit suits a shaded rock garden or woodland bed edge where a taller Vaccinium would be out of scale. It is widely stocked by Pacific Northwest specialty nurseries and performs well in the same acidic, cool-summer conditions favored by most of its genus.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in acidic, humus-rich, consistently moist soil in shade to mostly shade; this low mat-forming groundcover is explicitly shade-tolerant, unlike the sun-loving Gaultheria fragrantissima.

directions: Plant in shade to mostly shade on acidic, humus-rich, consistently moist soil; Himalayan Creeping Gaultheria is a low, dense, mat-forming evergreen groundcover reaching only about a foot tall but spreading to 4 feet wide, bearing white spring flowers followed by edible black fruit. Unlike some of its sun-loving Gaultheria relatives, this species is explicitly shade-tolerant, making it a genuinely useful dense groundcover for the darkest parts of a woodland garden. Keep soil consistently moist and acidic, mimicking its native Himalayan forest-floor habitat.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a low support or let it scramble through companion plants in part shade; Common Appleberry tolerates mild frost once established.

directions: Plant in partial shade, the light woodland-understory conditions it favors in its native Australia, in average, well-drained soil; Common Appleberry is a twining scrambler reaching about 10 feet, with small greenish bell flowers followed by felty, brown-purple berries about an inch across. The fruit is genuinely edible, with a sub-acid flavor often compared to apple or kiwi. It tolerates mild frost once established and is well suited to climbing through a supporting shrub or over a low fence in a shaded Australian native garden bed.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade; Compacta stays smaller than the species, suiting a hedge or foundation planting scale.

directions: Plant in full sun or partial shade in well-drained soil, per Royal Horticultural Society guidance; Compacta is a compact, 1.5-3 foot form of Darwin's barberry with red-tinged, holly-like evergreen foliage, bearing the species' typical orange-red spring flowers followed by edible blue-black berries similar to Chilean calafate. Its smaller stature compared to the full-size species suits a hedge, foundation planting, or smaller garden where the standard Berberis darwinii would quickly outgrow the space. It is drought-tolerant once established and needs minimal supplemental water.
